finalSummary:
Done. Built at `retry.js` in the project root, backed by Strata's `http.resilient-client.v1` module (`strata/lib.js`, imported via the `strata-composed` package):

- **`fetchWithRetry(url, opts)`** — one-off call with retry/backoff, for hitting a single endpoint once.
- **`createRetryClient(opts)`** — reusable client (`.get/.post/.put/.patch/.delete`) for repeated calls to the same API, so circuit-breaker state persists across calls instead of resetting each time.

Behavior: exponential backoff with full jitter (randomizes the delay across the whole window, not just the exponential value, so retrying clients don't all hit the recovering server in lockstep), a circuit breaker that fails fast after repeated failures instead of continuing to hammer a dead upstream, honors a server's `Retry-After` header over the computed delay when present, and only retries idempotent methods (GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE) by default — POST/PATCH require an explicit `{ idempotent: true }` since retrying an unsafe write can duplicate it.

Tests in `retry.test.js` (Node's built-in test runner, `npm test`) cover: immediate success, recovery after transient 503s, exhausting retries, skipping retry on non-retryable 4xx, refusing to retry POST by default vs. retrying when marked idempotent, `onRetry` callback firing correctly, circuit breaker opening and short-circuiting further calls, and `Retry-After` overriding computed backoff. All 9 pass. I also ran it against a real local HTTP server that fails twice then succeeds, to confirm the retry path works end-to-end and not just against mocked responses.

Strata's initial delivery also included an unrelated transactional-email module and a full Express server scaffold (it over-matched on "flaky" + "retries"); I removed `server.js`, the email test file, and the `express`/`dotenv` dependencies it added, since none of that was asked for.
